_comment: Scenario: UC-03-01 daytime bayshore traffic-jam monotony drive.
Derived from uc02_monotony_v0_1; tuned to fire the monotony_prevention band of
nri_fatigue_score_v1 on the 6.9 km Funabashi-Makuhari route.
Design (combined_contracts task-5-round2):
- trigger: nri_fatigue_score_v1 (NOT the hybrid trigger).
- traffic_jam_kph: 8 kph so 6.9 km crawls for ~52 min (18 ticks * 3 min/tick),
matching the UC brief: normally 20 min, stretches to 45-50 min in congestion.
- NRI score accumulation in full-route jam (familiar_route=true, is_night=false):
dS/dt = S_base(0.5*1.2=0.6/min) + S_jam(0.8/min) + S_mono(0.3/min)
= 1.7 pts/min = 5.1 pts per 3-min tick
threshold_monotony=60 crossed at ~tick 12 (~36 min)
threshold_fire=100 crossed at ~tick 20 (~60 min) -- AFTER route completes
- Route completes at tick 18 (~54 min): S_total ~= 91 pts, safely in [60,100).
Fire stays in monotony_prevention band; never escalates to rest_required.
- S_realtime = max(0, drowsiness-60)*1.5 + max(0, fatigue-60)*1.5.
With initial_state 5/5 and slow growth (~0.25/min drowsiness), both values
stay far below the theta=60 dead-band for the whole run (~20 at fire).
FATIGUE/DROWSINESS CONTRIBUTE ZERO to S_total. This is exactly the
'monotony not fatigue' story: the jam+familiar_route accumulation drives
the intervention, matching the persona's 'low departure fatigue' assumption.
- Scenario presets carry the jam event (start_min:0, duration:200 min)
so no jam_range_km override is needed from the test case.
- monotony_add_per_min kept at uc02 baseline (0.05): only affects the
drowsiness SIGNAL level, which stays <60 regardless -- reverted for honesty.
